symptom: `validation feedback $Input/Input_Person` — an ASSOCIATION written by its bare name — passes `check --references` and `exec`, then mx check fails **CE1613** "The selected attribute 'G45.Input.Input_Person' no longer exists." at Validation feedback activity 'Show validation message on member Input_Person of Input'. The qualified `$Input/G45.Input_Person` builds clean
cause: `addValidationFeedbackAction` split attribute from association by DOT COUNT alone: 0 dots = attribute, so a bare association name was always qualified as `Entity.Name` into AttributeName. The change-object writer (`resolveMemberChange`) already looked the bare name up in the domain model; validation feedback never got that lookup
insight: Same slot as #974 (inherited attribute → CE1613), one branch over: #974 fixed WHICH entity qualifies a bare attribute, and left the assumption that a bare name IS an attribute. When a writer chooses attribute vs association from the spelling's shape, ask what a dotless name can be — in MDL it is either. Resolution order: attribute in the generalization chain first (unchanged behaviour), then an association the entity or an ancestor OWNS (ParentID — searched in that link's own module, Associations AND CrossAssociations), else the old spelling so mxbuild still names it. Fixed output is byte-for-byte the qualified form's, so 'the qualified form builds' (the reporter's control) carries over; reproduced and cleared on 11.14.0 with two copies (pre-fix binary: the reported CE1613; fixed: 0 errors). Other bare-member writers that still decide by dot count are worth grepping for `strings.Count(` on a member name
